chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Yamani Corner is a door from the doors of Paradise; Allah did not close it since He opened it.
And in another report: 'It is our door to Paradise from which we enter.'

key_terms.الرُّكْنُ الْيَمَانِيُّ: The Yamani Corner, a specific corner of the Kaaba facing Yemen
key_terms.بَابُنَا: Our door (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the Yamani Corner in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the Yamani Corner is distinguished from the Black Stone as a unique portal of divine mercy, often interpreted as the specific entry point for the Ahl al-Bayt into Paradise, reflecting their elevated spiritual status. This narration underscores the theological significance of the Kaaba's corners not merely as ritual markers but as metaphysical gates connecting the earthly realm to the divine abode.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Yamani corner is a Door from the Doors of the Paradise. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> did not Lock it since He<sup>azwj</sup> Opened it’.
And in another report, ‘(He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘It is our<sup>asws</sup> Door to the Paradise from which we<sup>asws</sup> enter’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
al-Yemaniy corner is a door of the doors of paradise. Allah has not closed it from the day He opened it.”
In another Hadith it says, “It is our door to paradise through which we enter.”
